content.title: Hover a market row without changing layout
content.test_md_blob:
# Hover a market row without changing layout

> Prove the hover treatment does not change the hovered row height or move neighboring content.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a browser and wait until the ORBITAL single-page dashboard finishes rendering with the Market Overview section visible in the main workspace.

## Step 2

In the Market Overview section, store the NASDAQ row height as baseline_row_height and store the current positions of the S&P 500 row above it and the DOW row below it as baseline_neighbor_positions.

## Step 3

Hover the NASDAQ row in the Market Overview and keep the row hovered while its surrounding rows remain visible.

## Step 4

Assert the NASDAQ row height still equals baseline_row_height, and the S&P 500 and DOW rows still match baseline_neighbor_positions while the hover state is active.

## Step 5 — assert @verifies ac-97, ac-98

Confirm delta check: 0 (changed-by) — the stated promise: Hovering a market row does not change that row's height.

# Review the default market overview instrument set and row fields

> Prove the market overview shows the four required instruments and that each row exposes value, daily percentage, and sparkline.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a browser and wait until the ORBITAL single-page dashboard finishes rendering with the Market Overview section visible in the main workspace.

## Step 2

In the Market Overview section, inspect all visible market rows as a single set.

## Step 3

Assert the overview contains one row each for S&P 500, NASDAQ, DOW, and BTC/USD, with no extra market rows present.

## Step 4

Assert each of those four rows displays a current value, a daily percentage, and a sparkline.

## Step 5 — assert @verifies ac-89, ac-90, ac-91, ac-92, ac-93

Confirm count check: 4 (equals) — the stated promise: The market overview contains exactly four market rows.

# Refresh the same market overview state and confirm deterministic sparklines

> Prove the market overview re-renders the same sparkline traces for the same state because the sparklines use deterministic mock data.

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a browser and wait until the ORBITAL single-page dashboard finishes rendering with the Market Overview section visible in the main workspace.

## Step 2

In the Market Overview section, store the currently rendered sparkline traces for S&P 500, NASDAQ, DOW, and BTC/USD as baseline_sparklines.

## Step 3

Refresh the same browser page without changing any dashboard state, and wait until the Market Overview renders again.

## Step 4

Assert the sparkline traces for S&P 500, NASDAQ, DOW, and BTC/USD exactly match baseline_sparklines after the refresh.

## Step 5 — assert @verifies ac-94

Confirm absolute check: Sparkline traces for the four market rows match their baseline traces after a repeated render of the same market overview state. (equals) — the stated promise: Sparkline traces remain identical across repeated renders of the same market overview state.

    step: 3
  - objective: Assert the sparkline traces for S&P 500, NASDAQ, DOW, and BTC/USD exactly match baseline_sparklines after the refresh.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Scored highest because layout-shift regressions are subtle, user-visible, and directly violate the hover stability promises even when content still appears correct.
[value_score] Scored high because hover emphasis and sparkline enlargement are the primary interactive affordances of the market overview and are prone to styling regressions.
[value_score] Scored high because the baseline instrument set and per-row fields must be correct before any interaction can be meaningful.

[value_score] Scored moderate-high because deterministic sparklines protect trust in repeated observation and keep visual tests stable, but the defect is less immediately disruptive than missing content or layout shift.

[self_critique] The oracle proves the row-height promise directly with a pixel delta from baseline, and the surrounding-row assertion narrows the scope so the test does not over-claim whole-page immobility.

[self_critique] The technique fits the hover state-change promise, but the emphasized-state assertion remains somewhat broad because the source does not specify exact styling tokens; I kept it tied to visible change from the captured baseline and paired it with the concrete sparkline-size assertion.
[self_critique] The content test proves the exact instrument set and required row fields without assuming any unstated ordering, formatting, or extra metadata.

[self_critique] The repeated-render test proves deterministic sparklines for the same state by capturing a baseline before refresh and comparing like-for-like after refresh; no additional negative scenario is required because the source states only positive determinism, not alternative failure handling.
